manifest.name: dsh-folder-launcher
manifest.description: Add any folder to a running DeepSeek Harness Web workspace from Windows Explorer, starting dsh web automatically when needed.

bundle.text:
# dsh-folder-launcher bundle patch: inserts this plugin into a profile's layer stack.
#
# The plugin is a host-only DSH plugin. It registers two local routes on the
# composed web server and stores its discovery material under
# `$DSH_HOME/folder-launcher/`. Windows Explorer (or the cross-platform CLI)
# calls those routes to register a folder as a workspace.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-folder-launcher
      name: 'dsh-folder-launcher'

readme.text:
[中文](README.zh.md) | English

Add any folder to a **running** DeepSeek Harness Web workspace from the Windows Explorer context menu, and let it start `dsh web` automatically when needed. A small host plugin plus a per-user Explorer integration; no administrator rights, no restart of the running DSH instance, no editing `workspace.json`.

- Registers the folder through DSH's own `workspaceRegistry`, so the Web sidebar receives the workspace normally.
- Works without browser auth cookies: the launcher calls a loopback-only route protected by a local bearer token.
- Windows 7 / 8 / 10 / 11 compatible scripts (PowerShell 2.0 syntax); Windows 11 puts classic verbs under **Show more options** (`Shift+F10` opens the classic menu directly).
- Cross-platform Node CLI for Linux/macOS file managers and scripts.

> The DSH host itself requires Node 22; the Explorer scripts are Win7-compatible, but DSH may not run on Windows 7. See [requirements](README.zh.md#要求).

---

```text
Explorer right-click
   │  wscript.exe (no console flash)
   ▼
explorer/dsh-folder-launcher.ps1

Discovery files:

```text
$DSH_HOME/folder-launcher/state.ini   # pid / port / origin / startedAt
$DSH_HOME/folder-launcher/token       # 32-byte random hex token
```

`$DSH_HOME` defaults to `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh`.

---

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:snnnnke/dsh-folder-launcher#v0.1.0
```

No tag yet? Use the default branch:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:snnnnke/dsh-folder-launcher
```

Local development:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add file:D:\path\to\dsh-folder-launcher
```

Stop the running process (`Ctrl+C`) and start it again:

```powershell
dsh web
```

Verify the plugin published its state:

```powershell
Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\folder-launcher\state.ini"
```

A `git clone` contains the **whole repository**: the root has `install-context-menu.ps1` and the `explorer/` folder. You do not need to find the plugin under `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh`.

In a normal PowerShell (not elevated):

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/snnnnke/dsh-folder-launcher.git
cd dsh-folder-launcher
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install-context-menu.ps1
```

`cd dsh-folder-launcher` enters the clone you just created — not the plugin installation directory. If you cloned somewhere else, `cd` there or use the full path:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\your-clone\dsh-folder-launcher\install-context-menu.ps1"
```

`install-context-menu.ps1` is a root-level entry that calls `explorer\install.ps1`; running `.\explorer\install.ps1` directly is equivalent. The root entry just makes “clone, then install” obvious.

Do **not** run it elevated: the menu is per-user and is written to `HKCU`. Running as administrator writes to the administrator's account instead.

The installer writes only:

- `HKCU\Software\Classes\Directory\shell\DshFolderLauncher`
- `HKCU\Software\Classes\Directory\Background\shell\DshFolderLauncher`
- `HKCU\Software\Classes\Drive\shell\DshFolderLauncher`
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-folder-launcher\`

No `HKLM`, no admin.

The repository root is the DSH plugin; `explorer/` is the menu installer. `dsh plugin add github:...` installs only the plugin, never the menu. For the menu, clone or download the ZIP and run `install-context-menu.ps1` from the repository root. The installer copies the scripts it needs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-folder-launcher`; the clone can then be deleted or moved.

ZIP users: GitHub → **Code → Download ZIP** → extract → run `install-context-menu.ps1` in the extracted folder.

To simulate a network pull with a local bare repository (run in a normal PowerShell, not the DSH sandbox):

```powershell
cd D:\Code_stuff\harness_work
git clone --bare --branch main .\create .\gh-sim\dsh-folder-launcher.git
git clone --branch main .\gh-sim\dsh-folder-launcher.git .\pull-test\dsh-folder-launcher
cd .\pull-test\dsh-folder-launcher

Right-click a folder, folder background, or drive → **Add to DSH Web**.

If DSH Web is not running, the launcher starts `dsh web` directly (no confirmation) and returns immediately; a hidden background worker performs the add once the plugin is ready. DSH can take a minute or two to start with a heavy profile, so the Explorer action does not block. Toggle with `StartWebIfMissing` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-folder-launcher\config.ps1`.

---

Classic registry verbs appear under **Show more options**. Press **`Shift+F10`** for the classic menu directly. A true top-level Windows 11 menu needs a packaged `IExplorerCommand` COM server (MSIX sparse package, signing/developer mode); not included.

---

DSH core has **no official interactive terminal UI (TUI)**:

- The installed DSH ships a `web` profile; `headless` is a one-shot task, not an interactive terminal.
- There is no `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tui` on npm; `dsh tui` requires a separately installed third-party or custom profile.
- The old “Open terminal here” menu item only opened a terminal and never started DSH. It has been removed to avoid the misleading impression.
If you want a terminal UI, install a third-party TUI yourself and run it in a terminal; this project does not bundle or install one.

```powershell
node .\bin\dsh-folder-launcher.mjs add "D:\Code\my project"
node .\bin\dsh-folder-launcher.mjs health
node .\bin\dsh-folder-launcher.mjs state
```

On Linux/macOS, wire it into a file-manager custom action, for example:

```sh
node /path/to/dsh-folder-launcher/bin/dsh-folder-launcher.mjs add %f
```

---

The local route is outside DSH's browser `/api` fence and owns its own checks:

1. **Loopback only** — `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, or an IPv4-mapped loopback address.
2. **Bearer token** — persistent token in `$DSH_HOME/folder-launcher/token`.
3. **Origin rejected** — any request carrying an `Origin` header gets 403.
4. **Bounded body** — 16 KiB, `application/json` only.
5. **Directory validation** — absolute, existing directory; the actual registration uses `workspaceRegistry` (realpath-normalized).

Threat model: browser/CSRF protection, not protection from local malware running as the same user. Keep `DSH_HOME` and the token private. If DSH uses a self-signed TLS cert, the launcher skips certificate validation only for loopback HTTPS.

> If DSH is bound to a non-loopback address with `--host`, do not call the local route through that LAN address: the route accepts loopback sources only, and a LAN-IP request is refused with 403. The default `dsh web` bind (`127.0.0.1`) is the supported setup.

---

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\explorer\uninstall.ps1

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\explorer\uninstall.ps1 -RemoveData
```

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-folder-launcher
```

Restart `dsh web` afterwards.

---

```powershell
npm test
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\check-scripts.ps1
```

Tests cover route guards (401/403/404/405/413/415), idempotency, path validation, token comparison, discovery state, plugin `apply`/cleanup, and a fake-host integration that exercises the real plugin entry over HTTP.

Manual launcher test without a full DSH:

```powershell
node .\scripts\fake-host.mjs C:\temp\dsh-fake-home 0 C:\temp\marker.txt

$env:DSH_HOME = 'C:\temp\dsh-fake-home'
$env:DSH_FOLDER_LAUNCHER_NO_UI = '1'
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\explorer\dsh-folder-launcher.ps1 add "D:\some folder"
```

Real DSH end-to-end should run in a normal terminal (not inside a restricted DSH sandbox), because DSH spawns worker processes during boot.

Architecture: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md). Troubleshooting: [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md). Chinese details: [README.zh.md](README.zh.md).

---

- DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.0-0`.
- Windows 7 SP1+ for the Explorer scripts (PowerShell 2.0 syntax); validated for syntax and launcher flow on Windows 11 PowerShell 5.1. Windows 7 behavior should be verified on the target machine.
- Windows 11 top-level menu: not supported.
- Other OSes: plugin + Node CLI work; Explorer registry integration is Windows-only.
